title: Two-tier Agent Mail identity model — doctrine + wiring (ratified 2026-07-14)
description:
DECISION (Craig, 2026-07-14, this session): adopt the TWO-TIER identity model, replacing agent-identity.md's unwired mint-or-inherit doctrine. Rationale recorded so this isn't relitigated:
- Identity is the lock grain; the grain must match the WRITER-CONCURRENCY boundary. At PARALLEL_WIDTH>1 the parallel ac-implement children are independent concurrent writers in one shared checkout — inheriting one loop identity would put multiple writers under one name (forbidden by agent-identity.md's own corollary). Below the boundary, workers never commit/reserve, so per-worker identity is pure ceremony. The inherit model was written for a serial world; the width dial obsoleted it.
- TIER 1 (unique minted identity — mint via macro_start_session, reserve at work grain, release, self-deregister at exit): any session that CLAIMS BEADS or EDITS PRODUCT CODE — loop conductor (claims only), each ac-implement child, ac-review (auto-fix engineer edits code), ac-batch-close (fix-forward). Plan-family skills already conform.
- TIER 2 (FoggyCreek as EXPLICIT shared chore identity, not accidental fallback): serial low-contention writers — scheduled jobs (tidy/align/dream), ac-land sweep/report commits. HARD RULE = tier boundary AND safety guard: FoggyCreek may commit chore files but may NEVER claim beads or reserve files.
- Deregistration = 3 layers: (1) minter self-deregisters at own exit; (2) ac-land sweeps the identity roster handed by the loop (VERIFIED 2026-07-14 against live schemas: deregister_agent/retire_agent take registration_token as OPTIONAL — sweep by name works; force_release_file_reservation exists for stale holds); (3) next-run Phase-0 stale sweep + reservation TTL floor.
- Claim-visibility chain (CLAIM_ASSIGNEE threading + beads-closed-gate union + fail-closed) is solid and UNCHANGED by this epic.
Audit that produced this: 5 gaps — exit-land can't release/deregister identities never handed to it; stages never deregister; agent-identity.md contradicts live per-stage model; engineer wip-commit hatch collides with pre-commit guard; FoggyCreek fallback silently misattributes claims. Children implement; doctrine-rewrite child blocks the rest.

title: DECISION: cross-session identity deregistration mechanism — retire/deregister reject name-only calls at runtime (ac-ycr.5 premise falsified)
description:
## Context
ac-ycr.5 (deregistration layers 2+3) and agent-identity.md's Deregistration table rest on the epic-ratified premise ("verified against live schemas 2026-07-14"): retire_agent/deregister_agent take registration_token as OPTIONAL, so ac-land can sweep the handed roster BY NAME without token custody.

Runtime re-verification (ac-bead-refine round 2, 2026-07-16) contradicts this. The token IS optional in the SCHEMA (anyOf string/null, default null) — so the schema-level check was correct — but the tool REJECTS name-only calls at RUNTIME: "requires registration_token unless this MCP session has already authenticated as that agent." ac-land, and next-run ac-loop Phase 0, are freshly spawned sessions that never registered the roster's identities, so they hold no tokens for them. Cross-session retire/deregister BY NAME therefore fails. agent-identity.md's own "Call-scoped facts #1" already states tokens live with the minting session and do not transfer — consistent with the runtime rejection, inconsistent with the table's "sweep by name works" note.

Impact is narrow: ONLY cross-session IDENTITY deregistration (layer-2 identity-retire, layer-3 identity-retire). Sound and unaffected: layer-1 self-deregister (minting session holds its own token); force_release_file_reservation (schema + description confirm it releases ANOTHER agent's reservation by name via abandonment heuristics); reservation TTL floor (7200s). Note: there is NO TTL for identities today — only reservations expire.

## Options
- A. Roster carries tokens: children + loop report their registration_tokens (not just names) in summaries; ac-land retires by token. Cost: tokens transit summaries/prompts; agent-identity.md says tokens shouldn't transfer; mild secret-handling concern in a public-repo skill.
- B (recommended). Drop cross-session identity dereg; rely on layer-1 self-deregister for the happy path. ac-land layer-2 shrinks to force_release_file_reservation only (identities not retired cross-session). Accept that sessions which CRASH before self-deregister leave a retired-eligible identity with no automatic reaper (no identity TTL exists). Pair with option D as an upstream ask.
- C. ac-land re-registers (authenticates as) each roster identity, then deregisters it. Cost: hacky; resurrect-then-kill semantics unverified.
- D. Request an mcp-agent-mail capability: a project-scoped admin sweep that retires stale agents by name (a real cross-session teardown primitive). Cost: upstream dependency.

## Recommendation
B now (self-deregister is the honest primitive given the auth model; reservations still swept by force_release_file_reservation), and file D as an upstream ask so identity cleanup eventually gets a proper primitive. Once decided, reframe ac-ycr.5: layer-2 = force_release_file_reservation sweep only; identity cleanup = layer-1 self + (future) D. Also fold the ac-ycr.5 round-2 sub-finding here: ac-review/ac-batch-close delegation prompts never request their minted identity back, so those 2 of 5 Tier-1 identities never reach the roster anyway — under option B they self-deregister (layer 1), so roster omission is harmless; under A/C the delegation prompts would need to return the identity+token.

## Delivers
- decision: the chosen cross-session identity-cleanup mechanism recorded here, after which ac-ycr.5 is reframed to match and unblocked.
- doc: skills/_shared/agent-identity.md — the stale "verified against live schemas ... sweep by name works" paragraph (lines ~89-91) and Layer-2/3 Wiring cells corrected to the decided mechanism (the false premise this bead quotes and falsifies).

title: bug: verification-gate CLASS_RUNTIME silently under-fires — grep -qvE broken for multi-line ANY-match on macOS (ugrep/BSD)
description:
## Defect
`skills/_shared/verification-gate.md:70` classifies "any runtime code touched" with:
```
printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | grep -qvE '\.(md|mdx)$|\.test\.|\.spec\.|__tests__/|^\.github/|^docs/' && CLASS_RUNTIME=1
```
Combining `-q` (quiet, short-circuit) with `-v` (invert) does NOT yield ANY-non-matching-line semantics under the grep in use — `grep` here resolves to a **ugrep 7.5.0** shim (BSD-grep-like). `-qv` exits 0 only when EVERY line fails the pattern; on a mixed changeset it exits 1, so CLASS_RUNTIME stays 0 and the runtime verification gate SILENTLY skips — violating the "never silently skip / ambiguity counts as a match" invariant (same file, line 38).

## Empirical repro (verified live, RUN 20260719-185059-58770, 2026-07-19T16:53:03Z; artifact `/tmp/bead-work-refine-bxg-20260719-185059-58770/repro-ac-bxg.txt`)
```
P='\.(md|mdx)$|\.test\.|\.spec\.|__tests__/|^\.github/|^docs/'
printf 'a.ts\n'       | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 0  correct (runtime present)
printf 'x.md\n'       | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 1  correct (no runtime)
printf 'x.md\na.ts\n' | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 1  WRONG — a.ts is runtime, want 0
printf 'a.ts\nx.md\n' | grep -qvE "$P"; echo $?   # 1  WRONG — order-independent
```
Nearly every real changeset mixes runtime source with at least one .md/.test/.github/docs file → gate skips.

## Fix (target: `skills/_shared/verification-gate.md:70`, single line, single file)
Decouple `-q` from `-v`. Two forms, both verified correct under the failing shell (artifact above):
- **A (capture-and-test emptiness):**
  ```
  RT=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | grep -vE '<pattern>')
  [ -n "$RT" ] && CLASS_RUNTIME=1
  ```
- **B (decouple pipe):** `printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | grep -vE '<pattern>' | grep -q . && CLASS_RUNTIME=1`

Audit result: line 70 is the ONLY `-qv` (quiet+invert) combo in the file — the positive `-qE` matches on 54/55/58/59/61/64/67/178/179 are correct ANY-match semantics and need no change. Keep the existing fail-safe intent: ambiguous class errs toward runtime.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `skills/_shared/verification-gate.md` contains NO `grep -qv`/`-qvE` (quiet+invert) combo. Check: `grep -nE 'grep -[A-Za-z]*q[A-Za-z]*v|grep -[A-Za-z]*v[A-Za-z]*q' skills/_shared/verification-gate.md` returns nothing.
2. A mixed changeset sets CLASS_RUNTIME=1. Check: run the file's Step-1 block with `FILES=$'x.md\na.ts'` → `CLASS_RUNTIME=1`. (Also `a.ts\nx.md` → 1, order-independent.)
3. A docs/test-only changeset keeps CLASS_RUNTIME=0. Check: `FILES=$'x.md\ndocs/z.md'` → `CLASS_RUNTIME=0`; `FILES='a.ts'` → 1.
4. Behavior holds under the machine grep. Check: run AC2/AC3 with `grep --version` = ugrep 7.5.0 shim (this env), exit codes as above.

## Delivers
- `skills/_shared/verification-gate.md:70` — CLASS_RUNTIME classifier that fires on ANY runtime file in a mixed fileset (decoupled `grep -v` existence test), restoring the never-silently-skip invariant for every app that runs the verification gate on macOS/ugrep.

## Consumes
- none (standalone shared-doc fix; no blocker bead)

## Provenance

Shared skill — fix affects every app running the verification gate.

VALIDATION VERDICT (ac-g93, MistyDesert, 2026-07-19): read ~/mcp_agent_mail/src/mcp_agent_mail/app.py auth path.

FINDING: same-session token-free auth is (a) INTENDED-BUT-CONDITIONAL, NOT (b) 'never a guarantee' and NOT a clean upstream bug.
- register_agent (app.py:6021) and macro_start_session (app.py:9780) BOTH call _bind_session_agent, and _authenticate_agent (app.py:5154) returns token-free when _session_is_bound_to_agent is true. So the carry is a real designed mechanism.
- BUT the binding is keyed on a stable ctx.session_id (_session_binding_key, app.py:5050-5074). It fails in two ways our architecture hits: (1) each phase child is a SEPARATE MCP session that never inherits the conductor's binding; (2) transports that don't surface a stable session_id fall to a per-call orphan UUID (ctx refuses attribute caching), so the binding is written under one key and looked up under another -> invisible -> name-only call rejected. This exactly reproduces run 20260719-102946 (three independent children each rediscovering rejection).

CONCLUSION: our docs were OVER-CLAIMING the carry as dependable. It works only within one stable-session-id lifetime. Fix = always thread registration_token on every privileged call (blanket rule). No upstream bug filed: the mechanism is intentional and correct under a stable session id; issue #148 already fixed the HTTP variant. If a future repro proves failure WITHIN one confirmed-stable ctx.session_id, THAT would warrant an upstream file with this repro. Self-deregister (Layer 1, same session that registered) legitimately keeps the token-optional carve-out.

title: bug: beads-closed-gate completeness scope is identity-lifetime, not batch — later ceremonies re-demand prior batches' progress files (--beads batch scope needed)

title: Proposal: new mechanical ac-loop gates need a live multi-batch dry-run in their shipping ceremony (skills/ac-pipeline-builder/SKILL.md)
description:
## Decision memo
**Target:** skills/ac-pipeline-builder/SKILL.md (or a _shared testing-doctrine note) — the meta-skill governing how new mechanical pipeline gates ship.

**Evidence (RUN 20260719-185059-58770, cost: material):** The freshly-shipped ac-514 beads-closed-gate (skills/_shared/scripts/beads-closed-gate.sh) shipped with two scoping defects found only at live ceremony use, not by its unit tests: (1) single --progress file vs parallel-wave children -> ac-0wi; (2) identity-lifetime vs batch scope -> ac-0i1. Both fixed same-run but cost ~2 extra child-spawns + 2 ceremony delays. Root cause: the gate's unit tests did not exercise ac-loop's own documented multi-batch / parallel-wave run shapes.

**Proposed change:** Add a rule to ac-pipeline-builder: a new mechanical gate wired into ac-loop must include a live multi-batch dry-run against ac-loop's documented run shapes (parallel-wave, multi-batch identity-lifetime) in its OWN shipping ceremony, not just unit tests.

**Counter-argument (Phase 2 retrospective, sonnet analyst, full-context REJECT):** Both gaps cost ~1 CLI flag + a handful of tests each, were resolved within ~1 hour, folded into ceremonies already running, with zero reverts and zero incorrect output shipped. The bug-lane/fold-into-close mechanism is the intended cheap safety net for exactly this failure mode and worked as designed; adding pre-ship checklist weight may not produce a measured win over what already happened for free.

**Recommendation:** apply-modified or drop — Craig adjudicates. Filed because the friction carrier typed this material + confirmed-defect (mechanically clears the T2 bar); surfaced with the retrospective's counter so the gate decision is fully informed.
